answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently checked tasks show fraud or collusion. A kernel of trusted evaluators samples claims and publishes evidence, so one detected fake can trigger a ripple of audits across related identities rather than relying on names or IP addresses. Creating a nebula of Sybils is therefore costly: every identity ties up capital, and coordinated abuse risks losing it.
